dossier.purpose: Debian GNU/Linux as shipped for WSL: the manifest entry named 'Debian' in Microsoft's WSL distribution list (microsoft/WSL, distributions/DistributionInfo.json, read from master with no tag or commit). That entry points to Debian-project-hosted .wsl images (amd64 and arm64) on salsa.debian.org, each with a SHA-256. The other two sources are the Debian 13 'trixie' release page (lifecycle, architectures) and the Debian wiki's WSL guide. There is no source clone: the working directory holds only .round-meta.json, so only the three listed pages were read. Answer to the open question, from those pages: the manifest gives one Debian image per architecture. For x86_64 it is Debian_WSL_AMD64_v1.26.0.0.wsl (salsa.debian.org CI job 9606244), SHA-256 5ec7dc68216e75d1d4d4761474e99d8461a98d316537110314b137122a879e0f. The manifest names no Debian release, so 'this image is Debian 13' is an inference from the wiki ('Debian stable') and the release page (trixie 'declared stable'), not something the pages state.

claims.claim: Manifest group 'Debian' under ModernDistributions has exactly one entry: Name 'Debian', FriendlyName 'Debian GNU/Linux', Default true. No field names a Debian release (no '13' or 'trixie').
The manifest's top-level 'Default' key is 'Ubuntu', not Debian. The file carries no comments, license header, version field or date field (as fetched).

The legacy 'Distributions' list also has a 'Debian' entry: StoreAppId 9MSVKQC78PK6, Amd64PackageUrl and Arm64PackageUrl both https://publicwsldistros.blob.core.windows.net/wsldistrostorage/TheDebianProject.DebianGNULinux_1.12.2.0_neutral___76v4gfsz19hv4.AppxBundle, PackageFamilyName TheDebianProject.DebianGNULinux_76v4gfsz19hv4. No Sha256 field was listed for it.

Release page: 'Debian 13.7 was released on September 12th, 2026. Debian 13.0 was initially released on August 9th, 2025.' The page title is 'Debian "trixie" Release Information' and it says the release is 'declared stable'.

Release page lifecycle: 'The Debian 13 life cycle encompasses five years: the initial three years of full Debian support, until August 9th, 2028, and two years of Long Term Support (LTS), until June 30th, 2030. The set of supported architectures is reduced during the LTS term.' Further detail is deferred to the Security Information page (link target ../../security/, i.e. https://www.debian.org/security/) and https://wiki.debian.org/LTS (neither opened).

Architectures at initial release of trixie include 64-bit PC (amd64) and 64-bit ARM (AArch64), plus armhf, POWER (ppc64el), riscv64 and s390x. The page does not mention WSL, systemd, GPU/NVIDIA, Python/Node.js/Rust, checksums or signatures, or cloud/container images.

Wiki install: 'Install Debian: wsl --install -d Debian' (after 'wsl --set-default-version 2'). Older route: install the Debian app from the Microsoft Store; first start asks for a user and password, and that user gets sudo rights. Also: 'There is a way to install the Debian WSL distro offline & without using Microsoft Market' (linked to Microsoft Learn; no command given).

Wiki describes the image only as 'a Debian stable command line environment' (WSL1 or WSL 2). No release number is given. GUI apps need an update 'to Debian bookworm or later'. trixie and Debian 13 are never mentioned.

Wiki systemd procedure: add '[boot]' and 'systemd=true' to /etc/wsl.conf 'to activate systemd mode on next boot of WSL 2', then 'wsl --shutdown -d Debian' and restart with 'wsl -d Debian -u <username>'. 'WSL 2 with systemd is probably what you want... as WSL 2 is a prerequisite for GUI application support, and systemd is a prerequisite for many Debian packages.' The procedure says 'Reboot Windows 11' and notes 'a Windows 11 operating system for hosting WSL is assumed'.

Wiki Known Issues: 'Any software relying on systemd or low-level hardware accessibility might fail due to missing support from the current Windows kernel or virtualization interface.' No mention of NVIDIA, CUDA, GPU, Linux kernel versions, 'systemctl --user' or checksums.

Wiki FAQ: keep up to date 'as with any other Debian installation use apt/apt-get to install and update software from the official Debian mirrors (e.g., apt update && apt dist-upgrade)'. For a newer release: 'change your sources.list and upgrade your install as with every other Debian installation.'

Wiki dating and source: top note reads 'As of the time of writing, 2024-06-28, your best option for installing and using Debian GNU/Linux on WSL will probably be to use the WSL 2 subsystem and systemd mode.' Footer shows last modified 2026-03-13 21:54:12. App code and build dependencies are in the 'WSL repo on salsa' (https://salsa.debian.org/Debian/WSL, not opened); feedback goes through Microsoft Store reviews, IRC #debian-wsl on OFTC, or that repo.

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes, as WSL guest userland only. The manifest has an amd64 image (Amd64Url, Debian_WSL_AMD64_v1.26.0.0.wsl; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/WSL/master/distributions/DistributionInfo.json), and amd64 is a supported Debian 13 architecture (https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/). It is not an installer for a native Linux host: every documented procedure runs on Windows (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux).
platforms.wsl2: yes. The wiki documents 'wsl --set-default-version 2' then 'wsl --install -d Debian' and says 'WSL 2 with systemd is probably what you want' (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux). No listed page mentions WSL 2.7.13 or kernel 6.18, and the wiki names no kernel version, so compatibility with that exact host is not stated. The wiki assumes a Windows 11 host.
platforms.macos_arm64: no. WSL is a Windows feature: every documented step is PowerShell or dism.exe on Windows (wiki URL above) and no listed page mentions macOS. The manifest's Arm64Url is an arm64 WSL image for Windows hosts, not a macOS artifact.
platforms.gpu: unknown. None of the three listed pages mentions NVIDIA, CUDA or GPU compute, and the manifest has no GPU fields. The wiki covers only GUI apps (install mesa-utils on 'Debian bookworm or later') and warns that software relying on 'low-level hardware accessibility might fail due to missing support from the current Windows kernel or virtualization interface' (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux).

integrations.cli: Windows wsl.exe only: wsl --install -d Debian, wsl --set-default-version 2, wsl --shutdown -d Debian, wsl -d Debian -u <username>, wsl.exe --update (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux). No Debian-specific CLI is documented.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry or phone-home statement appears on any of the three pages. Network dependencies the pages show: (1) the manifest is hosted at raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/WSL/master (where it was read; whether wsl.exe fetches it from that URL at install time is not stated on the pages); (2) the image is downloaded from salsa.debian.org (job-artifact URL in the manifest), and the legacy Store package from publicwsldistros.blob.core.windows.net (DistributionInfo.json); (3) 'wsl.exe --update' and the Debian app come from the Microsoft Store (wiki, Install and systemd sections); (4) inside the distro, packages come from 'the official Debian mirrors' via apt (wiki FAQ). code.architecture: Not a code repository: the working directory is empty apart from .round-meta.json, so everything below comes from the three listed pages. Components: (1) microsoft/WSL distributions/DistributionInfo.json, a JSON manifest whose top-level keys are ModernDistributions (10 groups: Ubuntu, openSUSE, RLCPlus, SUSE, kali, Debian, AlmaLinux, archlinux, Fedora, eLxr), Default ('Ubuntu') and the legacy Distributions list (Store packages). The Debian group has one entry with Name, FriendlyName, Default, Amd64Url{Url,Sha256} and Arm64Url{Url,Sha256}. The manifest entry says only Name 'Debian' / FriendlyName 'Debian GNU/Linux' with no release field (DistributionInfo.json). The wiki says 'a Debian stable command line environment' and names only bookworm, as the minimum for GUI apps. The release page calls trixie 'declared stable' but never mentions WSL (https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/). The release and point release inside v1.26.0.0 are not stated anywhere I could read, and the image contents were not inspected.

The release page states a five-year life cycle: three years of full Debian support to 2028-08-09, then LTS to 2030-06-30 (https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/). The same page says 'The set of supported architectures is reduced during the LTS term' without listing which, so amd64 coverage during LTS is not stated there. The manifest does not tie the WSL image to Debian 13. The wiki says updates come from the official Debian mirrors via apt (FAQ).

The wiki documents enabling systemd by adding '[boot]' and 'systemd=true' to /etc/wsl.conf, effective on next WSL 2 boot (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux, WSL 2 with systemd support). It does not say whether the image enables systemd by default, and it never mentions systemctl --user or user services. Known Issues warns that software relying on systemd or low-level hardware accessibility 'might fail'.

No listed page mentions NVIDIA, CUDA or GPU compute: the Debian wiki WSL page and the trixie release page are silent, and the manifest has no GPU fields. Only GUI app support (mesa-utils) and the 'low-level hardware accessibility' caveat appear (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux).

The release page and the wiki name no package versions and do not mention Python, Node.js or Rust (https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/, https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux). The image contents were not inspected.

risks: Release identity not established. The manifest's Debian entry is just 'Debian' / 'Debian GNU/Linux' with no release field (DistributionInfo.json, ModernDistributions.Debian[0]). The wiki says only 'Debian stable' and 'bookworm or later' and never mentions trixie or Debian 13. The release page never mentions WSL. 'Image = Debian 13' is therefore an inference, and the point release inside the image is unstated (the wiki runs 'sudo apt update' and 'sudo apt dist-upgrade' after install). 'v1.26.0.0' in the file name appears to be the Debian WSL app version (the legacy Store package is 1.12.2.0), not a Debian release number. The wiki is also dated: its top note says 2024-06-28 and it still describes WSL1 and Windows 10 (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux, https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/).

Moving target. The project spec has no tag or commit, and the manifest on master has no version or date field as fetched. The Debian URL embeds CI job id 9606244 and v1.26.0.0, so a later manifest commit can change the URL and digest. Line numbers for the entry could not be established (fetch summaries disagreed), so it is cited by JSON path (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/WSL/master/distributions/DistributionInfo.json).

Hosting and checksum provenance. The image URL is a GitLab CI job-artifact path on salsa.debian.org ('/-/jobs/9606244/artifacts/raw/'), not a release page or mirror, and no listed page states artifact retention. The SHA-256 digests appear only in Microsoft's manifest. Neither Debian page mentions checksums, signatures or a verification command. I did not download the file or recompute its digest (DistributionInfo.json; https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/; wiki URL above).

Two Debian routes with different artifacts. The modern .wsl image (v1.26.0.0, with Sha256) and the legacy Store AppxBundle (1.12.2.0, StoreAppId 9MSVKQC78PK6, no Sha256 field listed). The wiki's older route is 'install the Debian app from the Microsoft Store'. The manifest's top-level Default is 'Ubuntu', so Debian must be requested by name (-d Debian). How wsl.exe 2.7.13 picks between the lists is not documented on the listed pages.

systemd is a manual post-install step in the wiki ('[boot] systemd=true' in /etc/wsl.conf, effective on next WSL 2 boot). The wiki does not cover systemctl --user or user services, or whether the image enables systemd by default. Its example 'sudo echo ... >> /etc/wsl.conf' performs the redirect in the unprivileged shell, so it may fail with a permission error (my reading of shell semantics, not tested); the wiki follows with a verify step. Known Issues warns that software relying on systemd or low-level hardware accessibility 'might fail' (wiki URL above).

Coverage gaps. None of the three pages says anything about NVIDIA/CUDA GPU use, Python / Node.js / Rust package versions, or compatibility with WSL 2.7.13 and kernel 6.18, so those needs cannot be confirmed from them (https://wiki.debian.org/InstallingDebianOn/Microsoft/Windows/SubsystemForLinux; https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/).

Long-term support detail is incomplete on the page read. Full support runs to 2028-08-09 and LTS to 2030-06-30, but 'The set of supported architectures is reduced during the LTS term' and the page does not list which. Details are deferred to the Security Information page and the Debian Wiki LTS section, which were not opened (https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/).

Licensing not stated. The manifest has no license header or field as fetched, and neither the release page body nor the wiki page gives a license. The license of the microsoft/WSL repository and of the packages inside the image was not read (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/WSL/master/distributions/DistributionInfo.json; https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/).
